proposed.text: An architectural firm assigned economic copyright in a building design to a developer. Five years later, the architect who created the design wants to claim authorship in professional materials. Which statement is most source-safe under RA 8293?

options.text: The developer owns all moral rights and can stop the architect from ever claiming authorship

The architect-author retains personal moral rights to claim authorship and attribution, while separate reproduction or publication uses may still depend on economic-rights permission or another legal basis
The architect can claim authorship only if the assignment was registered with IPOPHL
Moral rights exist only for three years after assignment

rationale.a: Economic copyright assignment does not assign moral rights.
rationale.c: Moral rights do not depend on IPOPHL registration in the local source.
rationale.d: Section 198 gives moral rights the author's lifetime plus 50 years after death, not three years.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 180 covers assignment of economic copyright. Sections 193 and 198 preserve personal moral rights, including attribution, and make them non-assignable and not subject to license. Section 195 allows only limited written waiver. The source-safe answer separates claiming authorship from reproducing or publishing copies controlled by economic rights.
rationale.takeaway: After economic assignment, the architect-author may still claim moral rights, but copying/publication uses require separate analysis.

proposed.explanation: Reframed to avoid unsupported blanket permission to publish building photographs after assignment.
